P1.evidence: P1a miss — the rep had the application and explicitly declined to use it: 'I saw your application, uh, but look, I'm a kind of old school guy, so I want to hear it from you.' Nothing was read back, and the opposite of 'feeling seen' happened when the rep opened by calling him the wrong name ('Uh, Caesar, correct?' / 'Arturo. Arturo.'). P1b miss — the four-part frame is never set. P1c miss — no frame agreement sought. P1d hit — clean and well-delivered open question: 'what's been going on, what you're trying to fix with fitness, health, and yeah, we'll go from there' followed by 'So brief me in, like, what's going on?'

P2.evidence: The best baseline in this batch by a distance. P2b hit — 'What do you do for...' surfaces both jobs and that both are on his feet. P2c hit — the rep actively probed the medical picture rather than letting it sit: 'What kind of medicine that you've been taking?', which produced the full list (Omeprazole, knee steroids, eye steroids, colon antibiotics, upcoming colonoscopy). P2d hit — explicit and correctly scoped: 'Apart from the knee that you mentioned, do you have any other injuries or anything that limits your movements?', plus duration established earlier with 'is it something just that's happened recently or that's been going on for longer?'. P2e hit — 'Do you exercise at like at all right now?' establishing two weekend sessions started two weeks ago. P2g hit — full day of eating walked through: 'could you walk me through how does your nutrition look like right now? Like, on a daily basis, what do you eat?'. P2h hit and the standout moment of the call — the rep reconstructed the schedule, asked 'What time do you actually go to bed?', then landed 'So we have around six hours of sleep. That's not a lot', which the prospect had genuinely never computed: 'Now that I think so, yes, it's not even six hours.' P2i hit — 'you tell me how it's actually affecting your day-to-day life, how you feel during the day'. P2a miss — age 45 was volunteered, height and weight never asked despite five years of unintended weight loss being disclosed. P2f miss — results from his prior heavy-lifting years never explored.

P3.evidence: Phase intent achieved — the rep got from 'I want to get in shape' to identity and fatherhood. P3f hit and rep-initiated rather than lucky: 'How can you be there for your son? How can you help him out if you cannot take care of yourself?', then reinforced 'He needs you more than ever, actually.' P3g hit — driven all the way to identity with the strongest question of the call, 'you said the person that you want to become, who's that Arturo from the future?', producing 'the person that I can give example to my son'. P3e hit — 'what would be possible when you actually make this work, when you become healthier?'. P3b/P3c/P3d partial — mobility and physique surfaced but largely prospect-led, and the explicit 'outside of the physical, what's driving this' bridge was never said in those terms. P3a miss — the one-thing-you-would-change question never asked. P3h miss — no reflect-back; the rep said 'That's powerful, man' but never closed the loop with 'so this isn't really about the weight, it's about being there for your son — is that right?', which was sitting right there.

P4.evidence: The weakest phase and a real gap. P4a/P4b/P4c miss — the rep never asked what he had tried before, what happened with it, or why it did not stick. This prospect had years of heavy gym training behind him and a friend who recommended kettlebells, all of it unexplored. P4d partial — the rep diagnosed the blocker himself rather than asking for it: 'with this schedule that you have right now, you need time to recover, you're working two jobs, that's a lot of pressure on your body, there is no time in your day to actually decompress.' Accurate, but the script wants the prospect to arrive there. P4e partial — the prospect did eventually name it unprompted ('I think I'm doing pretty much everything except I'm forgetting about me'), which the script credits only partially. P4f miss — the 'information isn't the problem, why can't you stick to it on your own' frame was never delivered, and here it would have been the wrong frame anyway, since his blocker is genuinely structural time scarcity rather than knowledge.

P5.evidence: P5a hit and near-verbatim: 'if nothing changes, and we're sitting here a year from now, two years from now, how do you think? Where does that lead you?' But the rep then abandoned the phase after one question. The prospect deflected into optimism ('No, I'm definitely ready for the change... I want to just become the person I want to be') and the rep accepted it rather than pressing. P5b miss — 'is that something you're willing to settle for?' never asked. P5c miss — no 'why not?', so the cost of inaction was never actually articulated by the prospect. P5d miss — no line-in-the-sand. Consequence was named but never made to hurt, and the prospect drifted straight into logistics about how many days a week he should train.

P6.evidence: P6b hit and cleanly answered: 'just to make sure, like, we're on the same page, if we can figure out all the details, are you fully committed to actually showing up and doing this work?' / 'Oh, yes.' P6c hit — the rep did wait for that yes before naming the price, and tied the price back to the identity work ('remember how we spoke about you getting to that new version of you, the new Arturo... to get you there, to be an example for your son, the full investment is 6K'). P6a miss — the belief question about structure and the right person in his corner was never asked, which matters here because the prospect's real doubt was never about willingness, it was about whether his body and his calendar allow it. SEQUENCING: as on the Erik Seman call, all three pillars were presented (00:24:08 to 00:32:19) BEFORE the commitment check (00:33:29), inverting the script's instruction to secure the verbal yes before presenting anything.

P11.evidence: Payment and onboarding were never reachable — the prospect deferred to his financial advisor and needed to renegotiate his work shifts, so no payment was attempted, no link sent and no agreement raised. Scored N/A rather than miss so the rep is not penalised for an unreachable phase. Credit where due on the handover instead: the rep booked the follow-up live rather than promising to email it, sent the invite during the call, and verified receipt — 'are you able to check in your email whether you got the invite? ... Because sometimes they go into spam folder and I don't want to, you know, you miss it.' That is exactly the P11 discipline applied to a rebooking.

objection_plays.detail: Two of the ten scripted moves ran. The rep asked for monthly surplus after bills ('how much on average is usually left at the end of each month?' / '$4,000') and for credit score ('do you know by any chance what's your credit score?' / '800'). Everything else was skipped: no isolation first ('finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%?'), no 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place', no cash on hand, no number of credit cards, no available credit per card, no used-versus-available, and no crypto/stocks question even though the prospect twice volunteered that his capital sits in an investment programme. Critically, the scripted line 'Most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up. Want to explore making it work?' was replaced with 'most of the guys just put it on a credit card up front' and a pivot to interest-bearing third-party finance. The rep also opened with 'But why'd you ask? Like you need a structured payment plan or something?', which invited the prospect to retract — and he immediately did: 'No, no, no. I just needed to know how is it that works.'

The third-party-consult trigger was present in substance — 'I have to talk with my financial advisor, then go from there' — but with a financial advisor rather than a spouse. The OB play adapts almost directly ('money aside, do you personally feel this CAN get you to your goal?', 'is this genuinely needing his input, or asking permission to bet on yourself?', 'when you talk to him, what obstacles might come up?'). None of it ran. The rep accepted the deferral immediately and moved to scheduling.

A think-about-it in substance across both money and schedule — 'I have to check it out, I have to check it out, that part' and 'I just need probably one or two weeks just to set up the schedule'. No OA move ran: no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now?' — which would have connected directly to the Arturo-from-the-future work the rep had already done twelve minutes earlier.

Timing was raised by the prospect ('I will say in a week, I just, I'm not going to fix this') and the rep agreed with it rather than working it. None of the OD moves ran — no 'things never slow down, when does it actually become the right time?', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets'. Notably the rep then added a two-week delay of his own by being on vacation until 9 August, so the call ends with both parties endorsing a fortnight of drift for a prospect whose stated blocker is that he never makes time for himself.
No fear or doubt about the modality; the prospect was already positively disposed via a friend's recommendation and had begun light kettlebell work himself.

SCRIPT GAP — the clinical-fit objection, and the single most important gap in the corpus. The prospect stated a direct physician instruction: 'the doctor told me not to lift heavy weights... He told me, just you got to go easy, just do a little cardio.' The playbook already records having no play for this (the Tyron Giuliani note), and it shows: the rep neither explored the scope of the restriction, nor asked whether kettlebell work sits inside or outside it, nor suggested clearing the programme with the physician, nor made the sale contingent on that. He acknowledged it and continued to a six-month loaded kettlebell offer. This is a script gap rather than a rep invention, but the outcome is that a man on daily acid-suppression medication with a colonoscopy the following week was quoted $6,000 with no clinical gate anywhere in the process.

SCRIPT GAP — no play for a prospect whose blocker is structural time scarcity rather than motivation or money. This prospect works two jobs across roughly fifteen hours a day, four to five days a week, and has one genuinely free day. The script's phases all assume a discretionary-time buyer. The rep improvised well (spotting the 15:00-16:30 gap between shifts, and the sleep debt) but the process offered him nothing, and the solution landed on the prospect cutting paid restaurant shifts to afford the time — a consequence nobody costed.

notes: Two calls in one. The baseline and goals work is the strongest in this batch — the sleep arithmetic and 'who's that Arturo from the future?' are both genuinely good, and the rep earned a clean commitment before naming price. Against that, three things need correcting and one is urgent. Urgent: a stated physician restriction on heavy lifting was heard and passed over; the rep must be required to seek clinical clearance before quoting, not after. Next: the money play was replaced with a third-party finance quote ($650 x 12 = $7,800) that is not an approved tier, and the rep's own phrasing 'why'd you ask? Like you need a structured payment plan or something?' talked the prospect out of surfacing his real constraint. Last: P4 was skipped entirely and the consequence frame was opened and abandoned after one question, which is why a highly motivated prospect left with a two-week delay and no decision.
